metadata.title: Multimodal AI.
metadata.note: Standalone teaching explainer (~3min). Narrator Muskan, @HumanitariansAI, banner 'AI, Explained'. FRAMEWORK-FIRST (built to pass PROOF): the reusable definition of multimodal is shown before any example (B01), then a worked example (B03), a falsifiability/edge case (B04: 'did the model SEE it, or read a transcript?'), and a scaffolded viewer task (B07). ONE insight: multimodal = one model that takes in AND connects more than one input type (text/image/audio/video) in the same context; the tell that catches fakes is whether the model saw/heard the original or just a converted transcript. Bookends render (composer/verdict/handoff/outro via Claude Remotion comps); body B01-B05 are house-style 4K PIL cards generated by make_cards.py.

beats.narration_text: Hey, I'm Muskan. Multimodal AI is everywhere right now, but most explanations stop at, it does text and images. Here's the useful version: it's a test you can run. By the end, you'll look at any tool and know if it's really multimodal, or just text with a converter taped on.

props.command: What actually makes an AI “multimodal” — and how do I tell the real thing from a text model with a converter bolted on?
output: one model, many kinds of input
the test: does it connect them?

beats.narration_text: Definition first, before any example. A model is multimodal when one model takes in more than one kind of input, text, image, audio, video, and connects them in the same context. Two words carry it: one model, and connects. Not four separate tools stapled together. One model, reasoning across all of it at once.

show.event: four input chips (text/image/audio/video) sit on the left
arrows converge into ONE model box, then a single answer on the right (accent on the model)

card.title: One Model, Many Senses.
card.subtitle: the definition, first
card.caption: multimodal = one model that takes in AND connects more than one kind of input, in the same context
card.footer: ONE MODEL · CONNECTS THE INPUTS · NOT FOUR TOOLS STAPLED TOGETHER

beats.narration_text: Here's what that looks like. Text: explain this report. An image: what's wrong with this diagram? Audio: summarize this meeting. Video: what happened in this recording? Same model, four kinds of input. Old AI needed a separate tool for each one. Multimodal takes them in one place.

show.event: the four ask-cards snap in, one per modality
caption lands: same model, four inputs

card.title: Four Kinds of Ask.
card.subtitle: same model, different input
card.caption: each is a different modality going IN — the model handles them in one place
card.footer: OLD AI: A SEPARATE TOOL PER INPUT · MULTIMODAL: ONE

beats.narration_text: Watch one run. You hand it a diagram and a question, what's wrong here? It doesn't just read your words. It looks at the image, finds the arrow pointing the wrong way, and answers about the picture. Input crossing from image to text, one connected answer. That's the definition, doing actual work.

show.event: an image tile AND a text question sit side by side, feeding the model
one answer prints, referencing the picture (the backwards arrow)

card.title: Watch One Run.
card.subtitle: image + text, connected
card.answer: “Step 3 feeds Step 2 — the arrow points the wrong way.”
card.caption: the model reads the picture and the question together, and answers about the picture
card.footer: IMAGE + TEXT IN · ONE CONNECTED ANSWER OUT

beats.narration_text: Now the test that catches fakes. A bolt-on setup runs your image through a converter, turns it into text, and feeds that text to a text-only model. The model never saw the picture. True multimodal, the model sees the pixels itself. So ask any tool one question: did it actually see the thing, or just read a transcript someone made of it?

show.event: left pipeline: image → converter → text → model (model never sees the image)
right pipeline: image → model directly (accent on the true path)

card.title: The Test That Catches Fakes.
card.subtitle: connected, or converted?
card.left_note: the model never saw the picture
card.right_note: the model sees the pixels itself
card.caption: if a converter turned your image into text first, the model never saw the picture — that’s not multimodal
card.footer: ASK: DID THE MODEL SEE IT — OR READ A TRANSCRIPT OF IT?

beats.narration_text: Why does this matter? Because real problems don't arrive as clean text. A doctor has a scan and notes. A factory has camera feeds, sensors, and logs. A developer has a screenshot, the code, and an error message. Multimodal meets the work where it already lives, mixed together.

show.event: five domain cards snap in, each showing its mix of inputs
caption lands: real work arrives mixed

card.title: Why It Matters.
card.subtitle: the world isn’t just text
card.caption: real problems arrive as a mix of inputs — multimodal meets the work where it lives

beats.narration_text: So next time you hear multimodal, run the test. One model, more than one kind of input, connected in one context. And ask the question that catches the fakes: did it actually see or hear the thing, or just read a transcript of it?

artifactLines: Definition: one model that takes in AND connects more than one input type — text, image, audio, video.
The tell: it reasons across inputs in one context, not four tools stapled together.
The fake: a converter turns image or audio into text first — the model never saw the original.
The test: ask “did the model see or hear it, or just read a transcript of it?”

beats.narration_text: Your turn, and this is a real test, not just go ask Claude. Take something from your week that mixed formats: a screenshot plus your question, or a voice note plus your notes. Hand it to a multimodal model and ask it to connect them. Then check, did it use the image or the audio, or quietly fall back to your words? Pause and run it.

props.command: Take something from my week that mixed formats — a screenshot plus my question, or a voice note plus my notes. Connect them into one answer. Then tell me: did you use the image or audio, or only my text?
output: check: did it use the image/audio?
or did it fall back to your words?
that check is how you catch a fake
